<div id="fof7bf5bb076bc41a89592cdd2127577b7"><ix:nonNumeric name="us-gaap:CashAndCashEquivalentsPolicyTextBlock" contextRef="D20251031" escape="true" id="Tag880">
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: left; text-indent: 45pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; line-height: 1.2;"><span style="font-family: 'times new roman', times; font-size: 10pt; line-height: inherit;"><i>Cash and Cash Equivalents</i> - Cash equivalents include certificates of deposit, U.S. Treasury bills and government money&#8211;market funds with maturities of <em style="font-style: inherit; font-variant: inherit; font-weight: inherit; font-stretch: inherit; line-height: inherit; font-optical-sizing: inherit; font-size-adjust: inherit; font-kerning: inherit; font-feature-settings: inherit; font-variation-settings: inherit;">90</em> days or less when purchased. Our cash balances are held at a few financial institutions and <em style="font-style: inherit; font-variant: inherit; font-weight: inherit; font-stretch: inherit; line-height: inherit; font-optical-sizing: inherit; font-size-adjust: inherit; font-kerning: inherit; font-feature-settings: inherit; font-variation-settings: inherit;"> may, </em>at times, exceed insurable amounts. We believe we help to mitigate this risk by depositing our cash in major financial institutions. At <em style="font-style: inherit; font-variant: inherit; font-weight: inherit; font-stretch: inherit; line-height: inherit; font-optical-sizing: inherit; font-size-adjust: inherit; font-kerning: inherit; font-feature-settings: inherit; font-variation-settings: inherit;"> <span style="line-height: inherit;" id="fs_OLG7RRX1I800000000000000000000FM">October 31, 2025</span> </em>and <em style="font-style: inherit; font-variant: inherit; font-weight: inherit; font-stretch: inherit; line-height: inherit; font-optical-sizing: inherit; font-size-adjust: inherit; font-kerning: inherit; font-feature-settings: inherit; font-variation-settings: inherit;"><span style="line-height: inherit;" id="fs_LFSNB8ZUXC00000000000000000000FM">2024</span></em>, $<ix:nonFraction name="us-gaap:CashEquivalentsAtCarryingValue" contextRef="I20251031" unitRef="USD" decimals="-5" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" id="Tag913">11.9</ix:nonFraction> million and $<ix:nonFraction name="us-gaap:CashEquivalentsAtCarryingValue" contextRef="I20241031" unitRef="USD" decimals="-5" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" id="Tag914">13.6</ix:nonFraction> million, respectively, of the total cash and cash equivalents was in cash equivalents and restricted cash equivalents.</span></p>





































































































































































 </ix:nonNumeric></div>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: left; text-indent: 45pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; line-height: 1.2;"><br/></p>
<div id="fo16e554199e134a4383394e64f30e66b1"><ix:nonNumeric name="us-gaap:FairValueOfFinancialInstrumentsPolicy" contextRef="D20251031" escape="true" id="Tag881">
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 45pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;"><span style="font-family: 'times new roman', times; font-size: 10pt; line-height: inherit;"><i>Fair Value of Financial Instruments</i> - The fair value of financial instruments is determined by reference to various market data and other valuation techniques as appropriate. Our financial instruments consist of cash and cash equivalents, restricted cash and cash equivalents, receivables, deposits and notes, accounts payable and other liabilities, customers<span style="color: #000000; font-family: 'times new roman', times; font-size: 13.3333px; font-style: normal; font-variant-ligatures: normal; font-variant-caps: normal; font-weight: 400; letter-spacing: normal; orphans: 2; text-indent: 0px; text-transform: none; widows: 2; word-spacing: 0px; -webkit-text-stroke-width: 0px; white-space: normal; text-decoration-thickness: initial; text-decoration-style: initial; text-decoration-color: initial; float: none; line-height: inherit; display: inline !important;">&#8217;</span> deposits, mortgage loans held for sale, nonrecourse mortgages, mortgage warehouse lines of credit, credit facilities, accrued interest and senior notes. The fair value of the credit facilities and senior notes is estimated based on the quoted market prices for the same or similar issues or on the current rates offered to us for debt of the same remaining maturities or when <em style="font-style: inherit; font-variant: inherit; font-weight: inherit; font-stretch: inherit; line-height: inherit; font-optical-sizing: inherit; font-size-adjust: inherit; font-kerning: inherit; font-feature-settings: inherit; font-variation-settings: inherit;">not</em> available, are estimated based on <em style="font-style: inherit; font-variant: inherit; font-weight: inherit; font-stretch: inherit; line-height: inherit; font-optical-sizing: inherit; font-size-adjust: inherit; font-kerning: inherit; font-feature-settings: inherit; font-variation-settings: inherit;">third</em>-party broker quotes or management<span style="color: #000000; font-family: 'times new roman', times; font-size: 13.3333px; font-style: normal; font-variant-ligatures: normal; font-variant-caps: normal; font-weight: 400; letter-spacing: normal; orphans: 2; text-indent: 0px; text-transform: none; widows: 2; word-spacing: 0px; -webkit-text-stroke-width: 0px; white-space: normal; text-decoration-thickness: initial; text-decoration-style: initial; text-decoration-color: initial; float: none; line-height: inherit; display: inline !important;">&#8217;</span>s estimate of the fair value based on available trades for similar debt instruments. The fair value of all of our other financial instruments approximates their carrying amounts.</span></p>





































































































































































 </ix:nonNumeric></div>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: left; text-indent: 45pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; line-height: 1.2;"><br/></p>
<div id="foac408a2589894d01b8c45eae4365de1b"><ix:nonNumeric name="us-gaap:InventoryPolicyTextBlock" contextRef="D20251031" escape="true" id="Tag890">
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: left; text-indent: 45pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; line-height: 1.2;"><span style="font-family: 'times new roman', times; font-size: 10pt; line-height: inherit;"><i>Inventories</i> - Inventories consist of land, land development, home construction costs, capitalized interest, construction overhead and property taxes. Construction costs are accumulated during the period of construction and charged to cost of sales under the specific identification method. Land, land development and common facility costs are allocated based on buildable acres to product types within each community, then charged to cost of sales equally based upon the number of homes to be constructed for each product type.</span></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: left; text-indent: 45pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; line-height: 1.2;"><br/></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: left; text-indent: 45pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; line-height: 1.2;"><span style="font-family: 'times new roman', times; font-size: 10pt; line-height: inherit;">We record inventories on our Consolidated Balance Sheets at cost unless the inventory is determined to be impaired, in which case the inventory is written down to its fair value. Our inventories consist of the following components: (<em style="font-style: inherit; font-variant: inherit; font-weight: inherit; font-stretch: inherit; line-height: inherit; font-optical-sizing: inherit; font-size-adjust: inherit; font-kerning: inherit; font-feature-settings: inherit; font-variation-settings: inherit;"><span style="line-height: inherit; display: inline;" id="fs_HGK95ZLKW000000000000000000000fs">1</span></em>) sold and unsold homes and lots under development, which includes all construction, land, capitalized interest and land development costs related to started homes and land under development in our active communities; (<em style="font-style: inherit; font-variant: inherit; font-weight: inherit; font-stretch: inherit; line-height: inherit; font-optical-sizing: inherit; font-size-adjust: inherit; font-kerning: inherit; font-feature-settings: inherit; font-variation-settings: inherit;"><span style="line-height: inherit; display: inline;" id="fs_EJH8RJDT1C00000000000000000000fs">2</span></em>) land and land options held for future development or sale, which includes all costs related to land in our communities in planning or mothballed communities; and (<em style="font-style: inherit; font-variant: inherit; font-weight: inherit; font-stretch: inherit; line-height: inherit; font-optical-sizing: inherit; font-size-adjust: inherit; font-kerning: inherit; font-feature-settings: inherit; font-variation-settings: inherit;"><span style="line-height: inherit; display: inline;" id="fs_XT277RC2NK00000000000000000000fs">3</span></em>) consolidated inventory <em style="font-style: inherit; font-variation-settings: inherit;">not</em> owned, which consists of model homes financed with an investor and inventory related to land banking arrangements accounted for as financings.</span></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: left; text-indent: 45pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; line-height: 1.2;"><br/></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: left; text-indent: 45pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; line-height: 1.2;"><span style="font-family: 'times new roman', times; font-size: 10pt; line-height: inherit;">We sell and lease back certain of our model homes with the right to participate in the potential profit when each home is sold to a <em style="font-style: inherit; font-variant: inherit; font-weight: inherit; font-stretch: inherit; line-height: inherit; font-optical-sizing: inherit; font-size-adjust: inherit; font-kerning: inherit; font-feature-settings: inherit; font-variation-settings: inherit;">third</em>-party at the end of the respective lease. As a result of our continued involvement and the ability to repurchase model homes with below market options, for accounting purposes in accordance with ASC <em style="font-style: inherit; font-variant: inherit; font-weight: inherit; font-stretch: inherit; line-height: inherit; font-optical-sizing: inherit; font-size-adjust: inherit; font-kerning: inherit; font-feature-settings: inherit; font-variation-settings: inherit;"><span style="line-height: inherit; display: inline;" id="fs_GLRTLFDN1C00000000000000000000fs">606</span>,</em> these sale and leaseback transactions are considered a financing rather than a sale. Our Consolidated Balance Sheets, at <em style="font-style: inherit; font-variant: inherit; font-weight: inherit; font-stretch: inherit; line-height: inherit; font-optical-sizing: inherit; font-size-adjust: inherit; font-kerning: inherit; font-feature-settings: inherit; font-variation-settings: inherit;"> <span id="fs_ML3QMQGGF400000000000000000000FM">October 31, 2025</span> </em>and <em style="font-style: inherit; font-variant: inherit; font-weight: inherit; font-stretch: inherit; line-height: inherit; font-optical-sizing: inherit; font-size-adjust: inherit; font-kerning: inherit; font-feature-settings: inherit; font-variation-settings: inherit;"><span style="line-height: inherit;" id="fs_WIYK45JHOW00000000000000000000FM">2024</span></em>, included inventory of $</span><ix:nonFraction name="hov:InventoryRealEstateOtherOptions" contextRef="I20251031_ModelSaleLeasebackFinancingArrangementsMember_HomeBuildingSegmentMember" unitRef="USD" decimals="-5" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" id="Tag945">74.3</ix:nonFraction><span style="font-family: 'times new roman', times; font-size: 10pt; text-indent: 45pt;">&#160;million and $</span><ix:nonFraction name="hov:InventoryRealEstateOtherOptions" contextRef="I20241031_ModelSaleLeasebackFinancingArrangementsMember_HomeBuildingSegmentMember" unitRef="USD" decimals="-5" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" id="Tag946">46.1</ix:nonFraction><span style="font-family: 'times new roman', times; font-size: 10pt; text-indent: 45pt;"> million, respectively, recorded to &#8220;Consolidated inventory </span><span style="font-family: 'times new roman', times; font-size: 10pt; text-indent: 45pt; font-style: inherit; font-variant: inherit; font-weight: inherit; font-stretch: inherit; line-height: inherit; font-optical-sizing: inherit; font-size-adjust: inherit; font-kerning: inherit; font-feature-settings: inherit; font-variation-settings: inherit;">not</span><span style="font-family: 'times new roman', times; font-size: 10pt; text-indent: 45pt;"> owned&#8221; with a corresponding amount of $</span><ix:nonFraction name="hov:LiabilitiesFromInventoryRealEstateNotOwned" contextRef="I20251031_ModelSaleLeasebackFinancingArrangementsMember_HomeBuildingSegmentMember" unitRef="USD" decimals="-5" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" id="Tag947">75.6</ix:nonFraction><span style="font-family: 'times new roman', times; font-variation-settings: inherit;">not</span><span style="font-family: 'times new roman', times; font-size: 10pt; text-indent: 45pt;"> owned&#8221; for the amount of net cash received from the transactions.</span></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: left; text-indent: 45pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; line-height: 1.2;"><br/></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: left; text-indent: 45pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; line-height: 1.2;"><span style="font-family: 'times new roman', times; font-size: 10pt; line-height: inherit;">We have land banking arrangements, whereby we sell our land parcels to a land banker and they provide us an option to purchase back finished lots on a predetermined schedule. Because of our options to repurchase these parcels, for accounting purposes, in accordance with ASC <em style="font-style: inherit; font-variant: inherit; font-weight: inherit; font-stretch: inherit; line-height: inherit; font-optical-sizing: inherit; font-size-adjust: inherit; font-kerning: inherit; font-feature-settings: inherit; font-variation-settings: inherit;"><span style="line-height: inherit; display: inline;" id="fs_R0N2JRBWHS00000000000000000000fs">606</span>,</em> these transactions are considered a financing rather than a sale. Our Consolidated Balance Sheets at <em style="font-style: inherit; font-variant: inherit; font-weight: inherit; font-stretch: inherit; line-height: inherit; font-optical-sizing: inherit; font-size-adjust: inherit; font-kerning: inherit; font-feature-settings: inherit; font-variation-settings: inherit;"> <span style="line-height: inherit;" id="fs_LIC30Q30AO00000000000000000000FM">October 31, 2025</span> </em>and <em style="font-style: inherit; <p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: left; text-indent: 45pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; line-height: 1.2;"><br/></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: left; text-indent: 45pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; line-height: 1.2;"><span style="font-family: 'times new roman', times; font-size: 10pt; line-height: inherit;">The recoverability of inventories and other long-lived assets is assessed in accordance with ASC <em style="font-style: inherit; font-variant: inherit; font-weight: inherit; font-stretch: inherit; line-height: inherit; font-optical-sizing: inherit; font-size-adjust: inherit; font-kerning: inherit; font-feature-settings: inherit; font-variation-settings: inherit;"><span style="line-height: inherit; display: inline;" id="fs_42TOTYO99C00000000000000000000fs">360</span>,</em> &#8220;Property, Plant and Equipment.&#8221; ASC <em style="font-style: inherit; font-variant: inherit; font-weight: inherit; font-stretch: inherit; line-height: inherit; font-optical-sizing: inherit; font-size-adjust: inherit; font-kerning: inherit; font-feature-settings: inherit; font-variation-settings: inherit;"><span style="line-height: inherit; display: inline;" id="fs_RJHL54KIF400000000000000000000fs">360</span></em> requires long-lived assets, including inventories, held for development to be evaluated for impairment based on the undiscounted future cash flows of the assets at the lowest level for which there are identifiable cash flows. We evaluate impairment at the individual community level, which is the lowest level of discrete cash flows that are available.</span></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: left; text-indent: 45pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; line-height: 1.2;"><br/></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: left; text-indent: 45pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; line-height: 1.2;"><span style="font-family: 'times new roman', times; font-size: 10pt; line-height: inherit;">We evaluate inventories of communities under development and held for future development for impairment when indicators of potential impairment are present. Indicators of impairment include, but are <em style="font-style: inherit; font-variant: inherit; font-weight: inherit; font-stretch: inherit; line-height: inherit; font-optical-sizing: inherit; font-size-adjust: inherit; font-kerning: inherit; font-feature-settings: inherit; font-variation-settings: inherit;">not</em> limited to, decreases in local housing market values, decreases in gross margins or sales absorption rates, decreases in net sales prices (base sales price, net of sales incentives), or actual or projected operating or cash flow losses. The assessment of communities for indication of impairment is performed quarterly. As part of this process, we prepare detailed budgets for all of our communities at least semi-annually and identify those communities with a projected operating loss. For those communities with projected losses, we estimate the remaining undiscounted future cash flows and compare those to the carrying value of the community, to determine if the carrying value of the asset is recoverable.</span></p>

<p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: left; text-indent: 45pt; font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt;"><br/></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: left; text-indent: 45pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; line-height: 1.2;"><span style="font-family: 'times new roman', times; font-size: 10pt; line-height: inherit;">These and other local market-specific conditions that <em style="font-style: inherit; font-variant: inherit; font-weight: inherit; font-stretch: inherit; line-height: inherit; font-optical-sizing: inherit; font-size-adjust: inherit; font-kerning: inherit; font-feature-settings: inherit; font-variation-settings: inherit;"> may </em>be present are considered by management in preparing projection assumptions for each community. The sales objectives can differ between our communities, even within a given market. For example, facts and circumstances in a given community <em style="font-style: inherit; font-variant: inherit; font-weight: inherit; font-stretch: inherit; line-height: inherit; font-optical-sizing: inherit; font-size-adjust: inherit; font-kerning: inherit; font-feature-settings: inherit; font-variation-settings: inherit;"> may </em>lead us to price our homes with the objective of yielding a higher sales absorption pace, while facts and circumstances in another community <em style="font-style: inherit; font-variant: inherit; font-weight: inherit; font-stretch: inherit; line-height: inherit; font-optical-sizing: inherit; font-size-adjust: inherit; font-kerning: inherit; font-feature-settings: inherit; font-variation-settings: inherit;"> may </em>lead us to price our homes to minimize deterioration in our gross margins, although it <em style="font-style: inherit; font-variant: inherit; font-weight: inherit; font-stretch: inherit; line-height: inherit; font-optical-sizing: inherit; font-size-adjust: inherit; font-kerning: inherit; font-feature-settings: inherit; font-variation-settings: inherit;"> may </em>result in a slower sales absorption pace. In addition, the key assumptions included in our estimate of future undiscounted cash flows <em style="font-style: inherit; font-variant: inherit; font-weight: inherit; font-stretch: inherit; line-height: inherit; font-optical-sizing: inherit; font-size-adjust: inherit; font-kerning: inherit; font-feature-settings: inherit; font-variation-settings: inherit;"> may </em>be interrelated. For example, a decrease in estimated base sales price or an increase in homes sales incentives <em style="font-style: inherit; font-variant: inherit; font-weight: inherit; font-stretch: inherit; line-height: inherit; font-optical-sizing: inherit; font-size-adjust: inherit; font-kerning: inherit; font-feature-settings: inherit; font-variation-settings: inherit;"> may </em>result in a corresponding increase in sales absorption pace. Additionally, a decrease in the average sales price of homes to be sold and closed in future reporting periods for <em style="font-style: inherit; font-variant: inherit; font-weight: inherit; font-stretch: inherit; line-height: inherit; font-optical-sizing: inherit; font-size-adjust: inherit; font-kerning: inherit; font-feature-settings: inherit; font-variation-settings: inherit;"><span style="line-height: inherit; display: inline;" id="fs_T3HELGKI7400000000000000000000fs">one</span></em> community that has <em style="font-style: inherit; font-variant: inherit; font-weight: inherit; font-stretch: inherit; line-height: inherit; font-optical-sizing: inherit; font-size-adjust: inherit; font-kerning: inherit; font-feature-settings: inherit; font-variation-settings: inherit;">not</em> been generating what management believes to be an adequate sales absorption pace <em style="font-style: inherit; font-variant: inherit; font-weight: inherit; font-stretch: inherit; line-height: inherit; font-optical-sizing: inherit; font-size-adjust: inherit; font-kerning: inherit; font-feature-settings: inherit; font-variation-settings: inherit;"> may </em>impact the estimated cash flow assumptions of a nearby community. Changes in our key assumptions, including estimated construction and development costs, sales absorption pace and selling strategies, could materially impact future cash flow and fair value estimates. Due to the number of possible scenarios that would result from various changes in these factors, we do <em style="font-style: inherit; font-variant: inherit; font-weight: inherit; font-stretch: inherit; line-height: inherit; font-optical-sizing: inherit; font-size-adjust: inherit; font-kerning: inherit; font-feature-settings: inherit; font-variation-settings: inherit;">not</em> believe it is possible to develop a sensitivity analysis with a level of precision that would be meaningful to an investor.</span></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: left; text-indent: 45pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; line-height: 1.2;"><br/></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: left; text-indent: 45pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; line-height: 1.2;"><span style="font-family: 'times new roman', times; font-size: 10pt; line-height: inherit;">If the undiscounted cash flows are more than the carrying value of the community, then the carrying amount is recoverable, and <em style="font-style: inherit; font-variant: inherit; font-weight: inherit; font-stretch: inherit; line-height: inherit; font-optical-sizing: inherit; font-size-adjust: inherit; font-kerning: inherit; font-feature-settings: inherit; font-variation-settings: inherit;">no</em> impairment is recorded. However, if the undiscounted cash flows are less than the carrying amount, then the community is deemed impaired and is written down to its fair value. We determine the estimated fair value of each community by calculating the present value of its estimated future cash flows at a discount rate commensurate with the risk of the respective community, or in limited circumstances, prices for land in recent comparable sale transactions, market analysis studies, which include the estimated price a willing buyer would pay for the land (other than in a forced liquidation sale), and recent bona fide offers received from <em style="font-style: inherit; font-variant: inherit; font-weight: inherit; font-stretch: inherit; line-height: inherit; font-optical-sizing: inherit; font-size-adjust: inherit; font-kerning: inherit; font-feature-settings: inherit; font-variation-settings: inherit;">third</em> parties. The estimated future cash flow assumptions are virtually the same for both our recoverability and fair value assessments. Should the estimates or expectations used in determining estimated cash flows or fair value, including discount rates, decrease or differ from current estimates in the future, we <em style="font-style: inherit; font-variant: inherit; font-weight: inherit; font-stretch: inherit; line-height: inherit; font-optical-sizing: inherit; font-size-adjust: inherit; font-kerning: inherit; font-feature-settings: inherit; font-variation-settings: inherit;"> may </em>be required to recognize additional impairments related to current and future communities. The impairment of a community is allocated to each lot on a relative fair value basis.</span></p>
<p style="margin: 10pt 0pt 0pt; text-align: left; text-indent: 45pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; line-height: 1.2;"><span style="font-family: 'times new roman', times; font-size: 10pt; line-height: inherit;">From time to time, we write off deposits, approval, engineering and capitalized interest costs when we determine that it is <em style="font-style: inherit; font-variant: inherit; font-weight: inherit; font-stretch: inherit; line-height: inherit; font-optical-sizing: inherit; font-size-adjust: inherit; font-kerning: inherit; font-feature-settings: inherit; font-variation-settings: inherit;">no</em> longer probable that we will exercise options to buy land in specific locations or when we redesign communities and/or abandon certain engineering costs. In deciding <em style="font-style: inherit; font-variant: inherit; font-weight: inherit; font-stretch: inherit; line-height: inherit; font-optical-sizing: inherit; font-size-adjust: inherit; font-kerning: inherit; font-feature-settings: inherit; font-variation-settings: inherit;">not</em> to exercise a land option, we take into consideration changes in market conditions, the timing of required land takedowns, the willingness of land sellers to modify terms of the land option contract (including timing of land takedowns), and the availability and best use of our capital, among other factors.</span></p>

<p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: left; text-indent: 45pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; line-height: 1.2;"><span style="font-family: 'times new roman', times; font-size: 10pt; line-height: inherit;">Inventories held for sale consists of parcels ready for sale in their current condition, where we have decided not to build homes but are instead actively marketing the parcels to potential buyers.&#160;<span style="font-size: 10.0pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman',serif; mso-fareast-font-family: 'Times New Roman'; mso-ansi-language: EN-US; mso-fareast-language: EN-US; mso-bidi-language: AR-SA;">As of&#160;&#160;October 31, 2025, there was <ix:nonFraction name="us-gaap:InventoryLandHeldForSale" contextRef="I20251031_HomeBuildingSegmentMember" unitRef="USD" decimals="-6" scale="6" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen" id="Tag953">no</ix:nonFraction> land held
for sale, compared to</span>&#160;$<ix:nonFraction name="us-gaap:InventoryLandHeldForSale" contextRef="I20241031_HomeBuildingSegmentMember" unitRef="USD" decimals="-5" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" id="Tag954">5.1</ix:nonFraction> million of land held for sale&#160;at <span id="fs_WC65BEFU4G00000000000000000000FM">October 31, 2024</span>. Land held for sale is reported at the lower of its carrying amount or fair value less costs to sell. In determining fair value for land held for sale, management considers, among other things, prices for land in recent comparable sale transactions, market analysis studies, which include the estimated price a willing buyer would pay for the land (other than in a forced liquidation sale) and recent bona fide offers received from outside third parties.</span></p>

<div style="line-height: 1.2;" id="foefe5f2a23a0f46f6b873c5bdddf700eb"><ix:nonNumeric name="hov:PostdevelopmentCompletionWarrantyCostsAndInsuranceDeductibleReservesPolicyPolicyTextBlock" contextRef="D20251031" escape="true" id="Tag885">
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: left; text-indent: 45pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; line-height: 1.2;"><span style="font-family: 'times new roman', times; font-size: 10pt; line-height: inherit;"><i>Warranty Costs and Construction Defect Reserves</i> - We accrue warranty costs that are covered under our existing general liability and construction defect policy as part of our general liability insurance deductible. This accrual is expensed in <span style="color: #000000; font-family: 'times new roman', times; font-size: 13.3333px; font-style: normal; font-variant-ligatures: normal; font-variant-caps: normal; font-weight: 400; letter-spacing: normal; orphans: 2; text-align: left; text-indent: 60px; text-transform: none; widows: 2; word-spacing: 0px; -webkit-text-stroke-width: 0px; white-space: normal; text-decoration-thickness: initial; text-decoration-style: initial; text-decoration-color: initial; float: none; display: inline !important;">&#8220;</span>Selling, general and administrative<span style="color: #000000; font-family: 'times new roman', times; font-size: 13.3333px; font-style: normal; font-variant-ligatures: normal; font-variant-caps: normal; font-weight: 400; letter-spacing: normal; orphans: 2; text-align: left; text-indent: 60px; text-transform: none; widows: 2; word-spacing: 0px; -webkit-text-stroke-width: 0px; white-space: normal; text-decoration-thickness: initial; text-decoration-style: initial; text-decoration-color: initial; float: none; display: inline !important;">&#8221;</span> homebuilding expenses.















<span style="font-size: 11pt; font-family: Aptos, sans-serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: left; text-indent: 45pt; line-height: inherit;"><span style="font-family: 'times new roman', times; font-size: 10pt; line-height: inherit;">For homes delivered in fiscal <span id="fs_LUWS8P7GZK00000000000000000000FM">2025</span>&#160;and&#160;<span id="fs_5KMT7W5V3K00000000000000000000FM">2024</span>,
our deductible under our general liability insurance was $<ix:nonFraction name="hov:GeneralLiabilityInsuranceDeductible" contextRef="I20241031" unitRef="USD" decimals="-5" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" id="Tag78"><ix:nonFraction name="hov:GeneralLiabilityInsuranceDeductible" contextRef="I20251031" unitRef="USD" decimals="-5" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" id="Tag933">30.0</ix:nonFraction></ix:nonFraction> million annually,
aggregated for construction defect and warranty&#160;claims. </span></span></span><span style="font-family: Aptos, sans-serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: left; text-indent: 45pt; line-height: inherit;"><span style="font-family: 'times new roman', times; font-size: 10pt; line-height: inherit;">As of November
1, 2023, we <span style="border-left: none; border-right: none;">no</span> longer have an aggregate deductible for bodily injury claims.
For bodily injury claims, our deductible per occurrence in
fiscal <span id="fs_Q26MPAM3OG00000000000000000000FM">2025</span>&#160;and&#160;<span id="fs_6NH34PWYHC00000000000000000000FM">2024</span>&#160;was $<ix:nonFraction name="hov:BodilyInjuryInsuranceDeductibleForActionOverClaims" contextRef="I20251031" unitRef="USD" decimals="-4" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" id="Tag934">0.25</ix:nonFraction> million and
$<ix:nonFraction name="hov:BodilyInjuryInsuranceDeductibleForActionOverClaims" contextRef="I20241031" unitRef="USD" decimals="-5" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" id="Tag935">0.5</ix:nonFraction> million for action over claims, respectively, both with a $<ix:nonFraction name="hov:BodilyInjuryInsuranceLimit" contextRef="I20241031" unitRef="USD" decimals="-5" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" id="Tag49"><ix:nonFraction name="hov:BodilyInjuryInsuranceLimit" contextRef="I20251031" unitRef="USD" decimals="-5" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" id="Tag936">30.0</ix:nonFraction></ix:nonFraction> million limit. </span></span><span style="font-family: 'times new roman', times; font-size: 10pt; line-height: inherit;">We do <em style="font-style: inherit; font-variant: inherit; font-weight: inherit; font-stretch: inherit; line-height: inherit; font-optical-sizing: inherit; font-size-adjust: inherit; font-kerning: inherit; font-feature-settings: inherit; font-variation-settings: inherit;">not</em> have a deductible on our workers' compensation insurance. Reserves for estimated losses for construction defects, warranty and bodily injury claims have been established using the assistance of a <em style="font-style: inherit; font-variant: inherit; font-weight: inherit; font-stretch: inherit; line-height: inherit; font-optical-sizing: inherit; font-size-adjust: inherit; font-kerning: inherit; font-feature-settings: inherit; font-variation-settings: inherit;">third</em>-party actuary. The <em style="font-style: inherit; font-variant: inherit; font-weight: inherit; font-stretch: inherit; line-height: inherit; font-optical-sizing: inherit; font-size-adjust: inherit; font-kerning: inherit; font-feature-settings: inherit; font-variation-settings: inherit;">third</em>-party actuary uses our historical warranty and construction defect data to assist management in estimating our unpaid claims, claim adjustment expenses and incurred but <em style="font-style: inherit; font-variant: inherit; font-weight: inherit; font-stretch: inherit; line-height: inherit; font-optical-sizing: inherit; font-size-adjust: inherit; font-kerning: inherit; font-feature-settings: inherit; font-variation-settings: inherit;">not</em> reported claims reserves for the risks that we are assuming under the general liability and construction defect programs. The estimates consider provisions for inflation, claims handling and legal fees. These estimates are subject to a high degree of variability due to uncertainties such as trends in construction defect claims relative to our markets and the types of products we build, claim settlement patterns, insurance industry practices and legal interpretations, among others. Because of the high degree of judgment required in determining these estimated liabilities, actual future costs could differ significantly from our currently estimated amounts. In addition, we establish a warranty accrual for lower cost-related issues to cover home repairs, community amenities and land development infrastructure that are <em style="font-style: inherit; font-variant: inherit; font-weight: inherit; font-stretch: inherit; line-height: inherit; font-optical-sizing: inherit; font-size-adjust: inherit; font-kerning: inherit; font-feature-settings: inherit; font-variation-settings: inherit;">not</em> covered under our general liability and construction defect policy. We accrue an estimate for these warranty costs as part of cost of sales at the time each home is closed and control is transferred to the buyer.</span></p>

<div id="fo32c520c715304acf90977e53ce3a6193"><ix:nonNumeric name="us-gaap:LandUnderOptionArrangementsPolicy" contextRef="D20251031" escape="true" id="Tag893">
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: left; text-indent: 45pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; line-height: 1.2;"><span style="font-family: 'times new roman', times; font-size: 10pt; line-height: inherit;"><i>Land Options -</i> We have access to land and lots through option contracts. Costs incurred to obtain options to acquire improved or unimproved home sites are capitalized. Such amounts are either included as part of the purchase price if the land is acquired or charged to &#8220;Inventory impairments and land option write-offs&#8221; if we determine we will <em style="font-style: inherit; font-variant: inherit; font-weight: inherit; font-stretch: inherit; line-height: inherit; font-optical-sizing: inherit; font-size-adjust: inherit; font-kerning: inherit; font-feature-settings: inherit; font-variation-settings: inherit;">not</em> exercise the option. We record costs associated with options on the Consolidated Balance Sheets under &#8220;Land and land options held for future development or sale.&#8221;</span></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: left; text-indent: 45pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; line-height: 1.2;"><br/></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: left; text-indent: 45pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; line-height: 1.2;"><span style="font-family: 'times new roman', times; font-size: 10pt; line-height: inherit;">In accordance with ASC <em style="font-style: inherit; font-variant: inherit; font-weight: inherit; font-stretch: inherit; line-height: inherit; font-optical-sizing: inherit; font-size-adjust: inherit; font-kerning: inherit; font-feature-settings: inherit; font-variation-settings: inherit;"><span style="line-height: inherit; display: inline;" id="fs_UQKWUMN7G000000000000000000000fs">810</span>,</em> &#8220;Consolidation,&#8221; we evaluate option contracts for land to determine whether they are with variable interest entities (<span style="color: #000000; font-family: 'times new roman', times; font-size: 13.3333px; font-style: normal; font-variant-ligatures: normal; font-variant-caps: normal; font-weight: 400; letter-spacing: normal; orphans: 2; text-align: left; text-indent: 60px; text-transform: none; widows: 2; word-spacing: 0px; -webkit-text-stroke-width: 0px; white-space: normal; text-decoration-thickness: initial; text-decoration-style: initial; text-decoration-color: initial; float: none; display: inline !important; line-height: inherit;">&#8220;</span>VIEs<span style="color: #000000; font-family: 'times new roman', times; font-size: 13.3333px; font-style: normal; font-variant-ligatures: normal; font-variant-caps: normal; font-weight: 400; letter-spacing: normal; orphans: 2; text-align: left; text-indent: 60px; text-transform: none; widows: 2; word-spacing: 0px; -webkit-text-stroke-width: 0px; white-space: normal; text-decoration-thickness: initial; text-decoration-style: initial; text-decoration-color: initial; float: none; display: inline !important; line-height: inherit;">&#8221;</span>)  and, if so, whether we are the primary beneficiary. A VIE is an entity in which either (i) the equity investors as a group, if any, lack the power through voting or similar rights to direct the activities of such entity that most significantly impact such entity&#8217;s economic performance or (ii) the equity investment at risk is insufficient to finance that entity&#8217;s activities without additional subordinated financial support. VIEs are consolidated when we have a controlling financial interest. A controlling financial interest will have both of the following characteristics: (a) the power to direct the activities of a VIE that most significantly impact the VIE&#8217;s economic performance and (b) the obligation to absorb losses of the VIE that could potentially be significant to the VIE or the right to receive benefits from the VIE that could potentially be significant to the VIE. If land and lot options are determined to be with VIEs and we are the primary beneficiary or the options have terms that require us to record it as a financing, then we record the land and lots under option on the Consolidated Balance Sheets under &#8220;Consolidated inventory <em style="font-style: inherit; font-variant: inherit; font-weight: inherit; font-stretch: inherit; line-height: inherit; font-optical-sizing: inherit; font-size-adjust: inherit; font-kerning: inherit; font-feature-settings: inherit; font-variation-settings: inherit;">not</em> owned&#8221; with an offset under &#8220;Liabilities from inventory <em style="font-style: inherit; font-variant: inherit; font-weight: inherit; font-stretch: inherit; line-height: inherit; font-optical-sizing: inherit; font-size-adjust: inherit; font-kerning: inherit; font-feature-settings: inherit; font-variation-settings: inherit;">not</em> owned.&#8221; We perform on-going re-assessments of VIEs based on subsequent events, such as the modification of contracts or other changes in facts and circumstances, which could cause our consolidation conclusions to change.</span></p>





































































































































































 </ix:nonNumeric></div>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: left; text-indent: 45pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; line-height: 1.2;"><br/></p>
<div id="fo6f3e8ba30e1b4c389ebd86ee4c1126c7"><ix:nonNumeric name="us-gaap:EquityMethodInvestmentsPolicy" contextRef="D20251031" escape="true" id="Tag886">
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: left; text-indent: 45pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;"><span style="font-family: 'times new roman', times; font-size: 10pt; line-height: inherit;"><i>Unconsolidated Homebuilding and Land Development Joint Ventures -</i> Investments in unconsolidated entities in which the Company has significant influence over the operating and financial decisions of the entity, but holds less than a controlling financial interest, are accounted for by the equity method. In all periods presented, our investments in unconsolidated homebuilding and land development joint ventures are accounted for under the equity method















<span style="font-size: 10.0pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman',serif; mso-fareast-font-family: 'Times New Roman'; mso-ansi-language: EN-US; mso-fareast-language: EN-US; mso-bidi-language: AR-SA;">because we are not the primary beneficiary or
de-facto agent, and we have a significant, but less than controlling, interest
in the entities.</span>&#160;Under the equity method, we recognize our proportionate share of income and loss earned by the joint venture upon the delivery of lots or homes to <em style="font-style: inherit; font-variant: inherit; font-weight: inherit; font-stretch: inherit; line-height: inherit; font-optical-sizing: inherit; font-size-adjust: inherit; font-kerning: inherit; font-feature-settings: inherit; font-variation-settings: inherit;">third</em> parties. Our ownership interests in joint ventures vary but our voting equity interests held are generally <ix:nonFraction name="hov:JointVentureVotingInterestPercentage" contextRef="I20251031_MinimumMember" unitRef="Pure" decimals="2" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" id="Tag911">20</ix:nonFraction>% to <ix:nonFraction name="hov:JointVentureVotingInterestPercentage" contextRef="I20251031_MaximumMember" unitRef="Pure" decimals="2" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" id="Tag912">50</ix:nonFraction>%. </span></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: left; text-indent: 45pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;"><br/></p>
<p style="text-indent: 45pt; line-height: 12pt; margin: 0in; font-size: 12pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', serif;"><span style="font-size: 10.0pt;">Specific criteria is used when determining if we are
the primary beneficiary of, or have a controlling interest in, an
unconsolidated entity. Factors considered in determining whether we have
significant influence, or we have control include risk and reward sharing,
experience and financial condition of the other partner, voting rights,
involvement in day-to-day capital and operating decisions and continuing
involvement. The evaluation of whether an entity is a variable interest entity
or a voting interest entity and then whether we are the primary beneficiary or
have control or significant influence can require significant judgment. We
believe that the equity method of accounting is appropriate for our investments
in unconsolidated entities where we are not the primary beneficiary and we do
not have a controlling interest but rather share control with our partners. In
most cases, the joint venture agreements require that both partners agree on
establishing the significant operating and capital decisions of the
partnership, including budgets, in the ordinary course of business.</span></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: left; text-indent: 45pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;"><br/></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: left; text-indent: 45pt; font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt;"><span style="font-family: 'times new roman', times; font-size: 10pt; line-height: inherit;">In accordance with ASC <em style="font-style: inherit; font-variant: inherit; font-weight: inherit; font-stretch: inherit; line-height: inherit; font-optical-sizing: inherit; font-size-adjust: inherit; font-kerning: inherit; font-feature-settings: inherit; font-variation-settings: inherit;"><span style="line-height: inherit; display: inline;" id="fs_CDUCJWN2CW00000000000000000000fs">323</span>,</em> &#8220;Investments - Equity Method and Joint Ventures,&#8221; we assess our investments in unconsolidated joint ventures for recoverability quarterly, and if it is determined that a loss in value of the investment below its carrying amount is other than temporary, we write down the investment to its fair value. We evaluate our equity investments for impairment based on the joint venture&#8217;s projected cash flows. This process requires significant management judgment and estimates.</span></p>





































































































































































 </ix:nonNumeric></div>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: left; text-indent: 45pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; line-height: 1.2;"><br/></p>
<div style="line-height: 1.2;" id="fo34cea3a1b9214494b1bee7a4a0e46c56"><ix:nonNumeric name="us-gaap:DeferredChargesPolicyTextBlock" contextRef="D20251031" escape="true" id="Tag897">
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: left; text-indent: 45pt; font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt;"><span style="font-family: 'times new roman', times; font-size: 10pt; line-height: inherit;"><i>Debt Issuance Costs -</i> Costs associated with our credit facilities and senior notes are capitalized and amortized over the respective term of the debt. The capitalized costs are recorded as a contra liability within our debt balances, except for the credit facility costs, which are recorded as a prepaid expense.</span></p>





































































































































































 </ix:nonNumeric></div>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: left; text-indent: 45pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; line-height: 1.2;"><br/></p>
<div style="line-height: 1.2;" id="fo9c68756cbfbc493ab55e9ac196593855"><ix:nonNumeric name="us-gaap:DebtPolicyTextBlock" contextRef="D20251031" escape="true" id="Tag895">
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: left; text-indent: 45pt; font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt;"><span style="font-family: 'times new roman', times; font-size: 10pt; line-height: inherit;"><i>Debt Issued at a Discount</i><i>/Premium</i><i> -</i> Debt issued at a discount or premium to the face amount is amortized utilizing the effective interest method over the respective term and recorded as a component of <span style="color: #000000; font-family: 'times new roman', times; font-size: 13.3333px; font-style: normal; font-variant-ligatures: normal; font-variant-caps: normal; font-weight: 400; letter-spacing: normal; orphans: 2; text-align: left; text-indent: 60px; text-transform: none; widows: 2; word-spacing: 0px; -webkit-text-stroke-width: 0px; white-space: normal; text-decoration-thickness: initial; text-decoration-style: initial; text-decoration-color: initial; float: none; display: inline !important; line-height: inherit;">&#8220;</span>Other interest<span style="color: #000000; font-family: 'times new roman', times; font-size: 13.3333px; font-style: normal; font-variant-ligatures: normal; font-variant-caps: normal; font-weight: 400; letter-spacing: normal; orphans: 2; text-align: left; text-indent: 60px; text-transform: none; widows: 2; word-spacing: 0px; -webkit-text-stroke-width: 0px; white-space: normal; text-decoration-thickness: initial; text-decoration-style: initial; text-decoration-color: initial; float: none; display: inline !important; line-height: inherit;">&#8221;</span> in the Consolidated Statements of Operations.</span></p>





































































































































































 </ix:nonNumeric></div>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: left; text-indent: 45pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; line-height: 1.2;"><br/></p>
<div style="line-height: 1.2;" id="fof98398f6460644f4851f365b9258fb0a"><ix:nonNumeric name="us-gaap:AdvertisingCostsPolicyTextBlock" contextRef="D20251031" escape="true" id="Tag882">
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: left; text-indent: 45pt; font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt;"><span style="font-family: 'times new roman', times; font-size: 10pt; line-height: inherit;"><i>Advertising Costs</i> - Advertising costs are expensed as incurred, primarily to <span style="color: #000000; font-family: 'times new roman', times; font-size: 13.3333px; font-style: normal; font-variant-ligatures: normal; font-variant-caps: normal; font-weight: 400; letter-spacing: normal; orphans: 2; text-align: left; text-indent: 60px; text-transform: none; widows: 2; word-spacing: 0px; -webkit-text-stroke-width: 0px; white-space: normal; text-decoration-thickness: initial; text-decoration-style: initial; text-decoration-color: initial; float: none; display: inline !important; line-height: inherit;">&#8220;</span>Selling, general and administrative<span style="color: #000000; font-family: 'times new roman', times; font-size: 13.3333px; font-style: normal; font-variant-ligatures: normal; font-variant-caps: normal; font-weight: 400; letter-spacing: normal; orphans: 2; text-align: left; text-indent: 60px; text-transform: none; widows: 2; word-spacing: 0px; -webkit-text-stroke-width: 0px; white-space: normal; text-decoration-thickness: initial; text-decoration-style: initial; text-decoration-color: initial; float: none; display: inline !important; line-height: inherit;">&#8221;</span> homebuilding expense in the Consolidated Statements of Operations. During the years ended <em style="font-style: inherit; font-variant: inherit; font-weight: inherit; font-stretch: inherit; line-height: inherit; font-optical-sizing: inherit; font-size-adjust: inherit; font-kerning: inherit; font-feature-settings: inherit; font-variation-settings: inherit;"> <span style="line-height: inherit;" id="fs_EP8JRYZG2O00000000000000000000FM">October 31, 2025</span>, </em><em style="font-style: inherit; font-variant: inherit; font-weight: inherit; font-stretch: inherit; line-height: inherit; font-optical-sizing: inherit; font-size-adjust: inherit; font-kerning: inherit; font-feature-settings: inherit; font-variation-settings: inherit;"><span style="line-height: inherit;" id="fs_KOZ0R8FCS000000000000000000000FM">2024</span></em> and <em style="font-style: inherit; font-variant: inherit; font-weight: inherit; font-stretch: inherit; line-height: inherit; font-optical-sizing: inherit; font-size-adjust: inherit; font-kerning: inherit; font-feature-settings: inherit; font-variation-settings: inherit;"><span style="line-height: inherit;" id="fs_HXYZ21MCKG00000000000000000000FM">2023</span></em>, advertising expenses totaled $<ix:nonFraction name="us-gaap:AdvertisingExpense" contextRef="D20251031" unitRef="USD" decimals="-5" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" id="Tag898">22.8</ix:nonFraction> million, $<ix:nonFraction name="us-gaap:AdvertisingExpense" contextRef="D20241031" unitRef="USD" decimals="-5" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" id="Tag889">17.2</ix:nonFraction> million and $<ix:nonFraction name="us-gaap:AdvertisingExpense" contextRef="D20231031_7" unitRef="USD" decimals="-5" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" id="Tag902">15.4</ix:nonFraction> million, respectively.</span></p>

<div id="fo24ec68bf61be419a85e7c3d6026d6865"><ix:nonNumeric name="us-gaap:IncomeTaxPolicyTextBlock" contextRef="D20251031" escape="true" id="Tag900">
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: left; text-indent: 45pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; line-height: 1.2;"><span style="font-family: 'times new roman', times; font-size: 10pt; line-height: inherit;"><i>Deferred Income Taxes -</i> Deferred income taxes are provided for temporary differences between amounts recorded for financial reporting and income tax purposes. If the combination of future years&#8217; income (or loss) combined with the reversal of the timing differences results in a loss, such losses can be carried forward to future years to recover deferred tax assets. In accordance with ASC <em style="font-style: inherit; font-variant: inherit; font-weight: inherit; font-stretch: inherit; line-height: inherit; font-optical-sizing: inherit; font-size-adjust: inherit; font-kerning: inherit; font-feature-settings: inherit; font-variation-settings: inherit;">740,</em> &#8220;Income Taxes,&#8221; we evaluate our deferred tax assets quarterly to determine if valuation allowances are required. We assess whether valuation allowances should be established based on the consideration of all available evidence using a &#8220;more-likely-than-<em style="font-style: inherit; font-variant: inherit; font-weight: inherit; font-stretch: inherit; line-height: inherit; font-optical-sizing: inherit; font-size-adjust: inherit; font-kerning: inherit; font-feature-settings: inherit; font-variation-settings: inherit;">not&#8221;</em> standard.</span></p>
<ix:exclude>

<p style="margin: 10pt 0pt 0pt; text-align: left; text-indent: 45pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; line-height: 1.2;"><span style="font-family: 'times new roman', times; font-size: 10pt; line-height: inherit;">In evaluating the exposures associated with our various tax filing positions, we recognize tax liabilities for more-likely-than-<em style="font-style: inherit; font-variant: inherit; font-weight: inherit; font-stretch: inherit; line-height: inherit; font-optical-sizing: inherit; font-size-adjust: inherit; font-kerning: inherit; font-feature-settings: inherit; font-variation-settings: inherit;">not</em> exposures on a quarterly basis. This evaluation is based on factors such as changes in facts or circumstances, changes in tax law, new audit activity by taxing authorities and effectively settled issues. Determining whether an uncertain tax position is effectively settled requires judgment. Such a change in recognition or measurement would result in the recognition of a tax benefit or an additional charge to the tax provision. A number of years <em style="font-style: inherit; font-variant: inherit; font-weight: inherit; font-stretch: inherit; line-height: inherit; font-optical-sizing: inherit; font-size-adjust: inherit; font-kerning: inherit; font-feature-settings: inherit; font-variation-settings: inherit;"> may </em>elapse before a particular matter for which we have established a liability is audited and fully resolved or clarified. We adjust our liability for unrecognized tax benefits and income tax expense in the period in which an uncertain tax position is effectively settled, the statute of limitations expires for the relevant taxing authority to examine the tax position or when more information becomes available. Due to the complexity of some of these uncertainties, the ultimate resolution <em style="font-style: inherit; font-variant: inherit; font-weight: inherit; font-stretch: inherit; line-height: inherit; font-optical-sizing: inherit; font-size-adjust: inherit; font-kerning: inherit; font-feature-settings: inherit; font-variation-settings: inherit;"> may </em>result in a liability that is materially different from our current estimate. Any such changes will be reflected as increases or decreases to <span style="color: #000000; font-family: 'times new roman', times; font-size: 13.3333px; font-style: normal; font-variant-ligatures: normal; font-variant-caps: normal; font-weight: 400; letter-spacing: normal; orphans: 2; text-align: left; text-indent: 60px; text-transform: none; widows: 2; word-spacing: 0px; -webkit-text-stroke-width: 0px; white-space: normal; text-decoration-thickness: initial; text-decoration-style: initial; text-decoration-color: initial; float: none; display: inline !important; line-height: inherit;">&#8220;</span>Income taxes<span style="color: #000000; font-family: 'times new roman', times; font-size: 13.3333px; font-style: normal; font-variant-ligatures: normal; font-variant-caps: normal; font-weight: 400; letter-spacing: normal; orphans: 2; text-align: left; text-indent: 60px; text-transform: none; widows: 2; word-spacing: 0px; -webkit-text-stroke-width: 0px; white-space: normal; text-decoration-thickness: initial; text-decoration-style: initial; text-decoration-color: initial; float: none; display: inline !important; line-height: inherit;">&#8221;</span> in the Consolidated Statement of Operations for the period in which they are determined. In addition, we record interest and penalties related to unrecognized tax benefits as a component of income tax expense. Accrued interest and penalties are included within <span style="color: #000000; font-family: 'times new roman', times; font-size: 13.3333px; font-style: normal; font-variant-ligatures: normal; font-variant-caps: normal; font-weight: 400; letter-spacing: normal; orphans: 2; text-align: left; text-indent: 60px; text-transform: none; widows: 2; word-spacing: 0px; -webkit-text-stroke-width: 0px; white-space: normal; text-decoration-thickness: initial; text-decoration-style: initial; text-decoration-color: initial; float: none; display: inline !important; line-height: inherit;">&#8220;</span>Income taxes payable<span style="color: #000000; font-family: 'times new roman', times; font-size: 13.3333px; font-style: normal; font-variant-ligatures: normal; font-variant-caps: normal; font-weight: 400; letter-spacing: normal; orphans: 2; text-align: left; text-indent: 60px; text-transform: none; widows: 2; word-spacing: 0px; -webkit-text-stroke-width: 0px; white-space: normal; text-decoration-thickness: initial; text-decoration-style: initial; text-decoration-color: initial; float: none; display: inline !important; line-height: inherit;">&#8221;</span> on the Consolidated Balance Sheets. </span></p>

<p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: left; text-indent: 45pt; font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt;"><span style="font-family: 'times new roman', times; font-size: 10pt; line-height: inherit;"><i>Prepaid Expenses -</i> Prepaid expenses that relate to specific communities (i.e., model setup, architectural fees, homeowner warranty program fees, interest rate buydowns, etc.) are charged to cost of sales as the applicable inventories are sold. All other prepaid expenses are amortized over a specific time period or as used and charged to overhead expense.</span></p>

<p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: left; text-indent: 45pt; font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt;"><span style="font-family: 'times new roman', times; font-size: 10pt; line-height: inherit;"><i>Allowance for Credit Losses</i> &#8211; We regularly review our receivable balances, which are included in <span style="color: #000000; font-family: 'times new roman', times; font-size: 13.3333px; font-style: normal; font-variant-ligatures: normal; font-variant-caps: normal; font-weight: 400; letter-spacing: normal; orphans: 2; text-align: left; text-indent: 60px; text-transform: none; widows: 2; word-spacing: 0px; -webkit-text-stroke-width: 0px; white-space: normal; text-decoration-thickness: initial; text-decoration-style: initial; text-decoration-color: initial; float: none; display: inline !important; line-height: inherit;">&#8220;</span>Receivables, deposits and notes, net<span style="color: #000000; font-family: 'times new roman', times; font-size: 13.3333px; font-style: normal; font-variant-ligatures: normal; font-variant-caps: normal; font-weight: 400; letter-spacing: normal; orphans: 2; text-align: left; text-indent: 60px; text-transform: none; widows: 2; word-spacing: 0px; -webkit-text-stroke-width: 0px; white-space: normal; text-decoration-thickness: initial; text-decoration-style: initial; text-decoration-color: initial; float: none; display: inline !important; line-height: inherit;">&#8221;</span> on the Consolidated Balance Sheets, for collectability. These include receivables from our insurance carriers, receivables from municipalities related to the development of utilities or other infrastructure, and other miscellaneous receivables. Allowances are maintained for potential credit losses based on historical experience, present economic conditions and other factors considered relevant. The allowance for credit losses were $<ix:nonFraction name="us-gaap:AllowanceForDoubtfulAccountsReceivable" contextRef="I20251031" unitRef="USD" decimals="-5" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" id="Tag932">12.9</ix:nonFraction> million and $<ix:nonFraction name="us-gaap:AllowanceForDoubtfulAccountsReceivable" contextRef="I20241031" unitRef="USD" decimals="-5" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" id="Tag903">13.0</ix:nonFraction> million at <em style="font-style: inherit; font-variant: inherit; font-weight: inherit; font-stretch: inherit; line-height: inherit; font-optical-sizing: inherit; font-size-adjust: inherit; font-kerning: inherit; font-feature-settings: inherit; font-variation-settings: inherit;"> <span style="line-height: inherit;" id="fs_BAY8VJTJ3400000000000000000000FM">October 31, 2025</span> </em>and <em style="font-style: inherit; font-variant: inherit; font-weight: inherit; font-stretch: inherit; line-height: inherit; font-optical-sizing: inherit; font-size-adjust: inherit; font-kerning: inherit; font-feature-settings: inherit; font-variation-settings: inherit;"><span style="line-height: inherit;" id="fs_C7YEWEWKEO00000000000000000000fs">2024</span></em>, respectively.</span></p>

<div style="line-height: 1.2;" id="fo9bdfff8b6d6b4e8f96cd8c9eafc9c953"><ix:nonNumeric name="us-gaap:ShareBasedCompensationOptionAndIncentivePlansPolicy" contextRef="D20251031" escape="true" id="Tag891">
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: left; text-indent: 45pt; font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt;"><span style="font-family: 'times new roman', times; font-size: 10pt; line-height: inherit;"><i>Stock-Based Compensation -</i> We account for our stock-based awards under ASC <em style="font-style: inherit; font-variant: inherit; font-weight: inherit; font-stretch: inherit; line-height: inherit; font-optical-sizing: inherit; font-size-adjust: inherit; font-kerning: inherit; font-feature-settings: inherit; font-variation-settings: inherit;">718,</em> &#8220;Compensation - Stock Compensation&#8221; which requires a fair-value based method to determine the estimated cost of an award. Compensation cost for stock-based awards is measured on the grant date. We recognize compensation cost for time-based awards ratably over the vesting period and performance-based awards ratably over the vesting period when it is probable that the stated performance target will be achieved. Forfeitures of stock-based awards are recognized as they occur.</span></p>

<div style="line-height: 1.2;" id="fo081854c00a5a455ea58639cf35406d7e"><ix:nonNumeric name="us-gaap:EarningsPerSharePolicyTextBlock" contextRef="D20251031" escape="true" id="Tag883">
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: left; text-indent: 45pt; font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt;"><span style="font-family: 'times new roman', times; font-size: 10pt; line-height: inherit;"><i>Per Share Calculations -</i> Basic earnings per share is computed by dividing net income (loss) (the <span style="color: #000000; font-family: 'times new roman', times; font-size: 13.3333px; font-style: normal; font-variant-ligatures: normal; font-variant-caps: normal; font-weight: 400; letter-spacing: normal; orphans: 2; text-align: left; text-indent: 60px; text-transform: none; widows: 2; word-spacing: 0px; -webkit-text-stroke-width: 0px; white-space: normal; text-decoration-thickness: initial; text-decoration-style: initial; text-decoration-color: initial; float: none; display: inline !important; line-height: inherit;">&#8220;</span>numerator<span style="color: #000000; font-family: 'times new roman', times; font-size: 13.3333px; font-style: normal; font-variant-ligatures: normal; font-variant-caps: normal; font-weight: 400; letter-spacing: normal; orphans: 2; text-align: left; text-indent: 60px; text-transform: none; widows: 2; word-spacing: 0px; -webkit-text-stroke-width: 0px; white-space: normal; text-decoration-thickness: initial; text-decoration-style: initial; text-decoration-color: initial; float: none; display: inline !important; line-height: inherit;">&#8221;</span>) by the weighted-average number of common shares outstanding, adjusted for participating securities (the <span style="color: #000000; font-family: 'times new roman', times; font-size: 13.3333px; font-style: normal; font-variant-ligatures: normal; font-variant-caps: normal; font-weight: 400; letter-spacing: normal; orphans: 2; text-align: left; text-indent: 60px; text-transform: none; widows: 2; word-spacing: 0px; -webkit-text-stroke-width: 0px; white-space: normal; text-decoration-thickness: initial; text-decoration-style: initial; text-decoration-color: initial; float: none; display: inline !important; line-height: inherit;">&#8220;</span>denominator<span style="color: #000000; font-family: 'times new roman', times; font-size: 13.3333px; font-style: normal; font-variant-ligatures: normal; font-variant-caps: normal; font-weight: 400; letter-spacing: normal; orphans: 2; text-align: left; text-indent: 60px; text-transform: none; widows: 2; word-spacing: 0px; -webkit-text-stroke-width: 0px; white-space: normal; text-decoration-thickness: initial; text-decoration-style: initial; text-decoration-color: initial; float: none; display: inline !important; line-height: inherit;">&#8221;</span>) for the period. Contingently issuable shares are included in basic earnings per share as of the date that all necessary vesting conditions have been satisfied. Computing diluted earnings per share is similar to computing basic earnings per share, except that the denominator is increased to include the dilutive effects of stock options and nonvested shares of restricted stock units (<span style="color: #000000; font-family: 'times new roman', times; font-size: 13.3333px; font-style: normal; font-variant-ligatures: normal; font-variant-caps: normal; font-weight: 400; letter-spacing: normal; orphans: 2; text-align: left; text-indent: 60px; text-transform: none; widows: 2; word-spacing: 0px; -webkit-text-stroke-width: 0px; white-space: normal; text-decoration-thickness: initial; text-decoration-style: initial; text-decoration-color: initial; float: none; display: inline !important; line-height: inherit;">&#8220;</span>RSUs<span style="color: #000000; font-family: 'times new roman', times; font-size: 13.3333px; font-style: normal; font-variant-ligatures: normal; font-variant-caps: normal; font-weight: 400; letter-spacing: normal; orphans: 2; text-align: left; text-indent: 60px; text-transform: none; widows: 2; word-spacing: 0px; -webkit-text-stroke-width: 0px; white-space: normal; text-decoration-thickness: initial; text-decoration-style: initial; text-decoration-color: initial; float: none; display: inline !important; line-height: inherit;">&#8221;</span>). Any stock options that have an exercise price greater than the average market price are considered to be anti-dilutive and are excluded from the diluted earnings per share calculation.  </span></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: left; text-indent: 45pt; font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt;"><br/></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 45pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;"><span style="font-family: 'times new roman', times; font-size: 10pt; line-height: inherit;">All shares that contain non-forfeitable rights to dividends or dividend equivalents that participate in undistributed earnings with common stock are considered participating securities and are included in earnings per share pursuant to the <em style="font-style: inherit; font-variant: inherit; font-weight: inherit; font-stretch: inherit; line-height: inherit; font-optical-sizing: inherit; font-size-adjust: inherit; font-kerning: inherit; font-feature-settings: inherit; font-variation-settings: inherit;"><span style="line-height: inherit; display: inline;" id="fs_K8RWYMQ3VK00000000000000000000fs">two</span></em>-class method. The <em style="font-style: inherit; font-variant: inherit; font-weight: inherit; font-stretch: inherit; line-height: inherit; font-optical-sizing: inherit; font-size-adjust: inherit; font-kerning: inherit; font-feature-settings: inherit; font-variation-settings: inherit;"><span style="line-height: inherit; display: inline;" id="fs_C8OLJ6W1MO00000000000000000000fs">two</span></em>-class method is an earnings allocation formula that determines earnings per share for each class of common stock and participating securities according to dividends or dividend equivalents and participation rights in undistributed earnings in periods where we have net income.</span></p>

<p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: left; text-indent: 45pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; line-height: 1.2;"><span style="font-family: 'times new roman', times; font-size: 10pt; line-height: inherit;"><i>Recent Accounting Pronouncements</i> - </span><span style="font-family: 'times new roman', times; ASU <em style="font-style: inherit; font-variant: inherit; font-weight: inherit; font-stretch: inherit; line-height: inherit; font-optical-sizing: inherit; font-size-adjust: inherit; font-kerning: inherit; font-feature-settings: inherit; font-variation-settings: inherit;"><span style="line-height: inherit; display: inline;" id="fs_QXSERCNQPS00000000000000000000fs">2023</span></em>-<em style="font-style: inherit; font-variant: inherit; font-weight: inherit; font-stretch: inherit; line-height: inherit; font-optical-sizing: inherit; font-size-adjust: inherit; font-kerning: inherit; font-feature-settings: inherit; font-variation-settings: inherit;"><span style="line-height: inherit; display: inline;" id="fs_QXJMTJ0DIO00000000000000000000fs">07</span></em> requires disclosure of significant segment expenses that are regularly provided to the chief operating decision maker and included within the segment measure of profit or loss. We adopted ASU 2023-07 for the year ended October 31, 2025, and applied it retrospectively to all prior periods presented in&#160;our Consolidated Financial Statements (see Note 10).</span></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: left; text-indent: 45pt; font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt;"><br/></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: left; text-indent: 45pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; line-height: 1.2;"><span style="font-family: 'times new roman', times; font-size: 10pt; line-height: inherit;">In December 2023, the FASB issued ASU <span style="line-height: inherit; display: inline;" id="fs_AYCALD382800000000000000000000FM">2023</span>-<span style="line-height: inherit; display: inline;" id="fs_AY8OPSFLS000000000000000000000FM">09</span>, &#8220;Improvements to Income Tax Disclosures&#8221; (&#8220;ASU <span style="line-height: inherit; display: inline;" id="fs_TM20G5M77K00000000000000000000FM">2023</span>-<span style="line-height: inherit; display: inline;" id="fs_MHD29OSINK00000000000000000000FM">09</span>&#8221;). ASU <span style="line-height: inherit; display: inline;" id="fs_DP3V0UCAHS00000000000000000000FM">2023</span>-<span style="line-height: inherit; display: inline;" id="fs_T2N5QUJ9GW00000000000000000000FM">09</span> requires enhanced disclosures related to the rate reconciliation and information on income taxes paid. This guidance will be applied prospectively and is effective for annual reporting periods in fiscal years beginning after December 15, 2024. We are currently evaluating the potential impact the adoption of this guidance will have on our Consolidated Financial Statements.</span><br/></p>
<p style="text-indent: 45pt; margin: 0in; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', serif; line-height: 1.2;"><span style="font-size: 10pt; line-height: inherit;"><br/></span></p>
<p style="text-indent: 45pt; margin: 0in; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', serif; line-height: 1.2;"><span style="font-size: 10pt; line-height: inherit;">In
November 2024, the FASB issued ASU 2024-03, &#8220;Disaggregation of Income Statement
Expenses&#8221; (&#8220;ASU 2024-03&#8221;). ASU 2024-03 requires disclosure of additional
information about specific cost and expense categories in the notes to the
financial statements. This guidance will be applied either prospectively or
retrospectively and is effective for annual reporting periods in fiscal years beginning
after December 15, 2026, and interim reporting periods in fiscal years
beginning after December 15, 2027. We are currently evaluating
the potential impact the adoption of this guidance will have on our
Consolidated Financial Statements.</span></p>

text-decoration-style: initial; text-decoration-color: initial; float: none; display: inline !important; line-height: inherit;">Intangibles - Goodwill and Other - Internal-Use Software (Subtopic 350-40): Targeted Improvements to the Accounting for Internal-Use Software</span><span style="color: #000000; font-style: normal; font-variant-ligatures: normal; font-variant-caps: normal; font-weight: 400; letter-spacing: normal; orphans: 2; text-align: left; text-indent: 60px; text-transform: none; widows: 2; font-variant-ligatures: normal; font-variant-caps: normal; font-weight: 400; letter-spacing: normal; orphans: 2; text-align: left; text-indent: 60px; text-transform: none; widows: 2; word-spacing: 0px; ASU 2025-06&#160;modernizes the accounting for the costs of internal-use software by removing all references to software development project stages so that the guidance is neutral to different software development methods. This guidance is effective for fiscal years beginning after December 15, 2027 and interim reporting periods within those annual reporting periods. Early adoption is permitted and the amendments in this update may be applied on a retrospective, modified transition, or prospective basis.&#160;We are currently evaluating the potential impact that the adoption of this guidance will have on our Consolidated Financial Statements.</span></span></p>

<div id="fs_GVSWASTETS00000000000000000000B"><ix:nonNumeric name="us-gaap:LesseeOperatingLeasesTextBlock" contextRef="D20251031" escape="true" id="Tag141">

<p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: left; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; line-height: 1.2;"><span style="font-family: 'times new roman', times; font-size: 10pt; line-height: inherit;"><b><em style="font-style: inherit; font-variant: inherit; font-weight: inherit; font-stretch: inherit; line-height: inherit; font-optical-sizing: inherit; font-size-adjust: inherit; font-kerning: inherit; font-feature-settings: inherit; font-variation-settings: inherit;">4.</em></b></span></p>

<td style="height: 17px;">
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: left; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;"><span style="font-family: 'times new roman', times; font-size: 10pt; line-height: inherit;"><b>Leases</b></span></p>
